title: Keeping the prompt short, direct and free of contradictory instructions

videos.script: A prompt grows. Somebody sees one bad answer and adds a line. Nobody ever deletes one. {{title}} This lesson starts from a prompt after a few weeks of that. It is eighteen lines long, and it costs ninety-eight tokens more than the version it grew from, on every call. {{long}} Two of its lines disagree. One asks for a brief summary. The other, added later, asks for the problem in full detail. Nobody can obey both, so the model picks. {{contradiction}} In the lab's stand-in the last line wins, and the summary turns into the whole message. A real model gives you no rule at all. {{summary}} You will find mistakes like that with a linter, and see what a linter cannot see. {{lint}} Then you cut the prompt back to eight lines and measure the cut. All forty answers stay the same, and the bill drops by more than a quarter. The pass count moves as well, and the sign test says that move is noise. {{compare}} By the end you can say what each line of a prompt is for, or you delete it. {{close}}
